mission_1.search: For BFS, the path length is 13.5 and expanded node count is 928. For A*, the path length is 13.5, and the expanded node count is 700.  The lengths are equal but A* examined fewer cells. BFS uses a FIFO deque, so it expands every cell at distance 1, then 2, and keep incrementing by 1 and spreads out in all directions, even the ones away from the goal, until frontier reaches it. While with A* it orders its heap by g+ ctx.heuristic(cell), so with this cells that are closer to the goal by Manhattan distance get a lower f and are therefore popped first. So, there are many cells that BFS would expand to that A* never touches. The lengths match because the Manhattan heuristic doesn't overestimate on a unit-cost grid. The goal test fires when the goal is popped, not when it is discovered, so the first time A* pops the goal it has the shortest path.
mission_1.failure:
One difference is that DFS expanded fewer cells than BFS (DFS: 598, BFS: 848) but returned a path that was around 3x longer (DFS: 74.5, BFS: 24.5). This is because my DFS uses a stack (stack.pop()), so it always continues from the most recently pushed cell. It goes down one route and returns the first path it hits, not the shortest one. While BFS's queue processes cells in order of distance, so its first path is the shortest. 

All four of the unreachable cases have a status of no_path. No_path means the search went through every reachable cell as much as it could and couldn't find a route. While resource_limit means that the search was stopped by the budget before it was finished, so there is no information on if there is a valid path or not. For example, IDDFS on both the open and constrained maps showed that a valid path existed but it ran out of budget, meaning too many expansions were called.

I used Claude to help me write some parts and debug my search implementations and to help explain certain parts I wasn't sure of. I caught a typo in my helper that I added and then fixed that. Additionally, I check the results myself by doing the small checks one by one for BFS to make sure they were working properly.
